metformin: Review baseline renal function (eGFR) prior to initiation and dose titration.
Administer with meals to minimize GI distress.
Hold 48 hours prior to and following iodinated IV contrast procedures.
amoxicillin: Dose adjust in moderate-to-severe renal impairment.
Complete full duration to prevent bacterial resistance emergence.
paracetamol: Maximum daily adult dose is 4,000 mg (2,000-3,000 mg in chronic liver disease or frail elderly).
Educate patients on hidden paracetamol in OTC cold and cough formulations.
atorvastatin: Advise patients to immediately report unexplained muscle tenderness, pain, or dark tea-colored urine.
Obtain baseline ALT/AST before starting therapy.
ramipril: Monitor serum creatinine and potassium 1-2 weeks after initiation and titration.
Warn patients about benign persistent dry cough; transition to ARB if intolerable.
furosemide: Monitor daily weights, blood pressure, serum electrolytes (K+, Na+), and renal parameters.
Prescribe morning dosing to avoid nocturnal polyuria.
spironolactone: Check serum potassium at Day 3, Day 7, and monthly for the first 3 months.
Advise against high-potassium diets and salt substitutes containing KCl.
ciprofloxacin: Maintain adequate patient hydration to prevent crystalluria in alkaline urine.
Separate oral administration from multivalent cations (dairy, antacids, iron) by at least 2 hours.
dapagliflozin: Counsel patients on genital hygiene to prevent mycotic infections.
Hold medication during acute surgical stress, critical illness, or prolonged fasting (EKA risk).
ondansetron: Screen for baseline prolonged QTc interval and hypomagnesemia before IV administration.
